  PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

Welcome to the meeting of the Parks, Recreation & Community Services Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs and videotapes of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling
(818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp.
PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request.
Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION
  MEETING MINUTES
  Monday, August 19, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
1.  ROLL CALL

  The meeting was called to order at 2:34 p.m.

  Present: Commissioners Babaian, Eberle, Kalfayan, Michals, and President Pro-Tem Wolfson
  Absent: None

  A.  Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the
  agenda for the August 19, 2019, regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall
  on or before Friday, August 16, 2019.
2.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  A. Introduction of New Commissioner, Kate Eberle
  Director of Community Services & Parks Onnig Bulanikian introduced Commissioner Eberle,
  providing information about her experience and community involvement. President Pro-Tem
  Wolfson welcomed her, and Commissioner Eberle said a few words.

  B.  Recognition of Cruise Night Sponsors
  Community Services Supervisor Norma Mower thanked everyone who supported Cruise Night, and
  said that the Cruise Night steering committee is open to receiving feedback to continue improving
  the event. She read the names of the event sponsors who were present at the meeting, and all
  Commissioners joined her at the podium to present certificates of recognition.

3.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
  Director of Community Services & Parks Onnig Bulanikian read a list of upcoming City Council agenda
  items related to the Community Services & Parks Department (CSP).

4.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Kalfayan congratulated staff for the completion of the Maple Park all-inclusive
  playground and commented on the success of the grand opening ceremony.

  Commissioner Michals acknowledged the end of the Concerts in the Park series held at Verdugo Park
  and thanked staff for their quick response in providing signage directing people to the parking lot
  directly across the street.

  President Pro-Tem Wolfson commented on the Cruise Night event and thanked everyone who
  contributed to the success of the event. She also commented on the grand opening ceremony of the
  Maple Park all-inclusive playground, saying that it was a beautiful ceremony and it was very meaningful
  to see all of the children playing in the new Shane’s Inspiration playground. She additionally inquired
  about the criteria for Commission consideration of items, because she noticed that on a recent Council
  agenda there was an item for bus service, and she didn’t remember the Commission having discussed

  1
   it at all. Deputy Director Aleksanian explained how staff generally determines what is brought before
  Commission.

  Community Services Supervisor Aylin Isayan, joined by Senior Services Committee Members Juan
  Gonzalez and Marie Filipian, announced an upcoming Emergency Preparedness event to be held on
  October 5 from 10 a.m. – 1 p.m. in the Police Community Room. She said that the event is geared
  towards seniors and their families, but open to the general public. Commissioner Michals asked if there
  will be a program or if it will be an open expo. Ms. Isayan said that the details of the event are still
  being planned, but that it will be an open expo, with meals served on site to congregate meals program
  participants.

  Ms. Moreno Hernandez announced upcoming events organized or sponsored by the Community
  Services & Parks Department.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker: James Gregory – Noise at Nibley Park
6.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on July 15, 2019.
  Moved:  Commissioner Kalfayan
  Seconded: Commissioner Babaian

  That the minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on July 15, 2019, be approved as
  written.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  Ayes:  Commissioners Babaian, Kalfayan, Michals, and President Pro-Tem Wolfson
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  Commissioner Eberle
7.  ACTION ITEMS
  A. Tree “Gender” in Glendale’s Urban Forest
  1.  Motion to note and file the report

  Deputy Director Koko Panossian provided some background for how this report came to be
  and introduced Urban Forester Loren Klick from Public Works, who gave a PowerPoint
  presentation covering the following: flower types of trees, City inventory, City policy, and field
  survey.

  Commissioner Michals thanked Mr. Klick for the report and asked if pollen/allergies factor into
  the selection of trees. He also asked for the Community Forest Plan to be presented to
  Commission once it has been updated.

  Moved:  Commissioner Kalfayan
  Seconded: Commissioner Michals

  That the Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Commission hereby notes and
  files the report regarding Tree “Gender” in Glendale’s Urban Forest.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  2
   Ayes: Commissioners Babaian, Eberle, Kalfayan, Michals, President Pro-Tem Wolfson
  Noes: None
  Absent: None
  Abstain: None

  B.  Aquatic Program Fees for Year-Round Programming
  1. Resolution eliminating various Summer Aquatics Program and swim lesson fees, adopting the
  eliminated fees under new names for year-round use, and establishing new fees for monthly
  pool entrance passes; and recommending that the Glendale City Council incorporate into the
  “Comprehensive Citywide Fee Schedule” the changes made to the CSP Department Wide Fee
  Schedule, effective October 1, 2019.

  Senior Community Supervisor Gabrielle Goglia provided a detailed report of the requested fee
  changes.

  Commissioners asked if staff has considered increasing fees due to the increase in minimum
  wage, what the revenue was the previous year, if the monthly pass will only be for non-
  summer months, and if the Summer Unlimited Pass will remain the same.

  Moved:  Commissioner Kalfayan
  Seconded: Commissioner Babaian

  That the Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Commission hereby approves the
  resolution as presented.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Babaian, Eberle, Kalfayan, Michals, President Pro-Tem Wolfson
  Noes: None
  Absent: None
  Abstain: None

8.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Citywide Sports Annual Report
  Ms. Goglia gave a PowerPoint presentation covering the following topics: citywide ballfields,
  contract class participation, drop in participation, field rentals, approved community youth sports
  groups, fiscal impact, and community outreach.

  Commissioners asked the following: if staff has explored how to address the drop in participation
  due to the use of Peach Jar by the school district; if staff had replied to the person who emailed the
  Commission regarding the use of sports fields; if staff has asked the Innovation, Performance, and
  Audit department to look at the community youth sports group policy; and if future reports can
  include information on closures due to maintenance and weather, as well as whether a field has
  natural or artificial turf.

  (Commissioner Kalfayan left the meeting at 3:51 p.m.)

  B.  One Glendale After School Youth Sports Program Annual Report
  Senior Community Supervisor Sevag Garabetian gave a PowerPoint presentation covering the
  following topics: program participants and goals, benefits, sponsors, program details, GO!
  Program, game times and locations, how outcomes are measured, performance measures, One
  Glendale Sports Experiences, additional support, and program budget.

  3
   C.  Section Activity Reports
  1.  Workforce Development
  Workforce Development Administrator Judith Velasco reported on the Measure H Paid Work
  Experience Program for homeless clients, announced the upcoming Tech Job Fair, said that
  Workforce Development will be launching a bioscience and biotechnology industry credentials
  program, and will continue to provide Computer Numeric Control machinist training to
  individuals with disabilities.

  2.  Human Services
  Senior Community Services Supervisor Maggie Kavarian provided an update on the Senior
  Services Committee’s first year. She gave a PowerPoint presentation covering the following
  topics: background and history of the Committee, 6 key recommendations resulting from the
  Senior Needs Assessment, formation of the Senior Services Committee, Committee actions
  taken at its four meetings in FY 2018-2019, and upcoming meetings in FY 2019-2020.

  3.  Recreation & Community Services
  Mr. Garabetian gave a PowerPoint presentation covering the following July events and
  programs: Cruise Night, Dive-In movie in honor of Parks Make Life Better Month, Let’s Play
  Day, Summer Concerts in the Park, programs in community centers, Therapeutic Recreation,
  Youth & Family Services, STAR, and Trails & Open Space.

  4.  Park Services
  Mr. Panossian provided a brief overview of work orders completed by Park Services staff in
  the month of July.

9.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at 4:25 p.m.
